guide.name: Copy of A Guide to LibGuides

asset.description:
LG2 Documentation Page
LibGuide Examples

This guide's purpose is to help you create and edit LibGuides. The basics of are included in Creating a Guide, Basics of Editing, and Design Tips. For an admin level account please see For Admins. Here, the LibGuides does an overview of the levels of organization and customization you can use when creating guides. This includes groups and templates.

<!-- Web2PDF Converter Button BEGIN --> <script type="text/javascript"> var pdfbuttonlabel="Save page as PDF" </script> <script src="http://www.web2pdfconvert.com/pdfbutton2.js" id="Web2PDF" type="text/javascript"></script> <!-- Web2PDF Converter Button END -->

When you first log into your LibGuides account go to the top left of the screen and choose LibGuides from the pull down menu

From here you can create a guide or edit an existing guide. Select Create Guide to begin

                        

 

You can add in all of the necessary information here. Start by assigning the guide to a group--ALWAYS USE RESOURCE BLUEPRINT UNLESS TOLD OTHERWISE

 

If you want, you can copy the content of an existing guide and use this as template or you can start fresh. End by adding a Guide Name (which you can change later) and selecting "Create Guide" at the bottom of the screen

Now that you have created a guide take these initial first steps:

Change the guide from Unpublished to Published - this allows you to send the URL to show others. If the guide is unpublished, no one will be able to view your guide even with a URL

Change the URL to a a friendly URL. Select the pencil icon next to the URL underneath your guide title. Here you can make a friendly URL. If you want to change the URL of the individual pages, do this by clicking the pencil icon next to the Page URL on the individual pages (you must change the guide URL before you can change the Page URL)

The top level is the guide itself. Within the guide you have both pages and subpages. In these pages you have boxes. Within these boxes you add the content (text, links, images, videos, etc). This gives you a large space to organize all of your ideas and content. Keep in mind your audience!

Add a page by clicking on the plus icon below the page names on the left hand side of your edit screen

A screen similar to this one will appear where you can add a name, description and a position. Here, you can make the page a sub-page of another page. 

             

 


You can also reuse an existing page by selecting the "Reuse Existing Page" tab at the top. Here, you will select the guide you want the page from, and the page within the guide you want. You have two options. By selecting the box next to copy, you have created a separate page, meaning any changes to the original page will not be made to yours. This way, you can edit this page. If you do not check the box, any page made to the original will also change yours and you will not be allowed to edit the new page.

If you decide later you want to move the position of page, you can by selecting page next to the page URL, and selecting Pages under Reorder/Move.

You can drag and drop the pages here. 

If you decide to change the name of your page after it has been created, go to the same Page icon next to the Page URL and select Page Properties. Here you can change the Page Name and Description.

The next level of organization is boxes. You can add boxes in a variety of places. Your screen should like similar to this:

These correspond to where your boxes will be placed:

You can always rearrange the boxes after you have created them by selecting Page > Reorder/Move > Boxes

Once you select Add Box you will see a screen similar to this:

 Here you can add the box name and change the box type. The main box types you will be using are standard, tabbed and gallery. Standard is just a single standard box. Tabbed creates tabs for you that can name and add content. This expands your workspace area if you have a lot of content. Gallery acts as a carousel that automatically cycles through images which you can title, add captions and link to sites.

At any time you can change the box name by clicking on the pencil icon at the top right corner of the box.

 

When you select Add Box you can select the tab at the top which says Reuse Existing Box. This allows you to pull any box from any guide. 

Select the guide you want to copy the box from and then the box name. You can change the name of the box on your guide. By selecting Copy, you are simply copying the box. If you do not choose this then this is a mapped box meaning you can only edit the box on the original site. This is useful if you have important information you use on several guides and only want to edit it on one guide.

Once you have added a box you can add content. Select the Add/Reorder box to get a pulldown menu of your options. 

The majority of your content will be Rich Text/HTML. Here you can type as though you are in word. You can add tables, images, links, etc. This will be your best friend in LibGuides and the most used tool. You can change color, font, size, etc.

Adding a database allows you to search LibGuides for a database that a librarian has created. You can add a description and change where tis description appears (as a hover, under the title, etc). This is good when you want to add a link to a database and want space to include descriptions. 

A link does exactly what it says. You can create a link name, link URL and description and then choose where this description appears. You can also add links in the Rich Text/HTML option. If you do it through Link you cannot edit font size, type and color.

Media/Widget has a space where you can add code. This can be an embed code from a YouTube channel or a widget you found an another website. If you are interested or know about HTML coding this is a useful tool. You can also reuse existing widgets by selecting that tab when the box appears.

Book from the Catalog allows you to search for a books ISBN and add all relevant details including a description and icon (cover art). 

Document/File allows you to upload a document/file from your computer and allow users to access this. You can again add titles, descriptions and cover art (icon). 

RSS Feed requires you to insert an RSS Feed URL. Like any RSS Feed this will automatically update on your site. 

Poll allows you to create a question and answer options and let your viewers answer the poll and see the responses.

Google Search lets you insert an automatic Google Search (including Scholar and Images). Place a keyword to appear in your search. 

 

You can reorder your content by selecting Reorder Content at the bottom of this pull down menu. Drag and drop the content and when satisfied, remember to press Save.
To change the Guide Name at any time just click on the title on the edit screen and a text box appears where you can change the title:
When you first create a guide it is important to make the guide's group: Resource Blueprint. If you forget to do this select the gear icon on the edit screen and select Change Type & Group.

If you would like someone else with a LibGuides account to have access to edit your guide you can do this by selecting the gear icon at the top your edit screen.

Search for their name and select Save. 

Note: If you do not see someone's name this means that their account was not set up properly. Try having them check their account information by clicking their email address in the top right hand corner. Here they can change their settings. On this page their first and last name MUST be filled in in order to be visible in the guide editors screen.

asset.description:
If you want to add a search bar that searches across all of the LibGuides, add content-->add media/widget

In the embed code add the following:

If you are looking to make an image gallery, unfortunately there is no set way to do this in LibGuides. Try this as an alternative:

 

You could upload the images as smaller icons the way I previously mentioned. You could make them small and line them up that way. You could make the images links and these could link to another LibGuide that has only the image but much larger, taking up all of column 1.

With the text/caption overlay is there a way to change the font color as the white blends in with the background image?

You can add it to the guides Custom JS/CSS box:

  1. ​While editing the guide, go to the mini menu in the upper right hand corner, choose the image icon, and choose Guide Custom JS/CSS.
  2. Add this:
    <style>
    .carousel-caption { color: #333; }
    </style>
    You can make the #333 any color you want; #333 is dark gray.
  3. Click Save.
When you edit the document there is a way to change the image (and its size)-- go to the Assign Thumbnail Image section, click to expand. Here, you can add a url and change its dimensions.

If you want to change the size of your guide title click the image icon on the top right and select Custom JS/CSS.
 
Insert this:
<style>
h1#s-lg-guide-name {font-size:50px; }
</style>
 
After font size, change this to any size that you like.

You can insert custom CSS code into a box from another site, your own code, etc. To do this add content-->add media/widget and place the code in the embed code box. Some examples are as follows:

This code was used: <div id="s-lg-content-11239634" style="text-align:center" class="  clearfix">
                <h4><span style="font-family:verdana,geneva,sans-serif;">Current Conditions at UMass Lowell provided by the UML Atmospheric Department</span></h4>
           </div>
            <div id="s-lg-content-10312809"  style="text-align:center" class="s-lg-widget ">
 <img src="http://storm.uml.edu/~metweb/UMLStorm/images/forecast.jpg" alt="Image 01" width="75%" height="95%"/> </a>
           </div>

To add the 5-day weather forecast from the UML Atmospheric Department. Whenever they update their site, this guide automatically updates:

You can add a video by going to add conetnt-->add media/widget

In the embed code box, copy the embed code from the YouTube video. This is found underneath the YouTube video under share-->embed

Copy this code. You can change the width and height of the video by changing the pixels in the copied code.

If you would like to create an A-Z bar like the one here: 

You must take advantage of the anchor tool in the rich text editor window. This is the flag icon:

First navigate to the place you want the link to take you on the page (for example, if you want to click D on the A-Z bar, navigate to the beginning of the D section of the page). Here click the anchor icon next to the text you would want the link to go to. In the anchor name, call it something simple and straightforward you will remember (for example, d).

Now, navigate back to the D at the top of the A-Z bar. Highlight the D and add a link (click the link button in the editor menu). Add the link for the page that your D section is on. Immediately after the URL type #d. This will take you to where the placed the "d" anchor.

box.name: Important Tips to Keep in Mind

asset.description:
Here’s a list of tips I have been given and have passed on to others using this platform:

1. Use Verdana size 14 for most of the text (make sure this is normal text, not a heading)
 
2. Use bold and italics to your advantage
 
3. To do single spacing press shift while you enter
 
4. If you want to create links to anything (including databases) you can either do this by adding text or adding links. When you add text instead this allows you to edit the style (font, bold, size, etc) which proves to be more useful in the end. It is almost always better to add text for nearly everything.
 
5. The group shows the box name so you do not need to retype the name in the text
 
6. When you add images by right clicking and going into the properties you can align the box to the right, left or center and also change the size
 
7. To avoid lengthy pages of scrolling you can reorder boxes by putting them into different columns. Select page at the top menu--reorder---boxes. Drag the boxes to different columns to spread out content.
 
8. Columns 2 and 3 do not display headings. This comes in handy when you want to split the page between text and an image and just have one title. Add a title in column 1 above the two boxes.
 
9. Format doesn’t always cross over the way you think. Click the eye icon to see a preview of what the page would actually look like
 
10. When the use the built in numbering/bulleting when you add rich text you can’t easily change the style of the numbers. Instead manually type the numbers when you want a numbered list.
For more help see the Springshare site where you can access information just for Admins

As an administrator you have abilities that extend beyond editing the LibGuide. You can create groups and templates. In a group you have to ability to change the general look including box colors, heading colors, header and footer options, etc. Within this group you assign it a template. The template is where you can change the general layout of the page including proportions of boxes, number of boxes, etc. Check out the groups and templates sub-pages to get the most from LibGuides. 

To access your administrator settings look at your LibGuides main menu at the top. Navigate to the Admin button, which will present a drop down menu where you can explore your settings.

As you work with LibGuides you will find that technical difficulties may arise. Here are some some common inquiries that I have been asked about. 

Why don't I see my peer's name when I try to add them as a guide editor?

I clicked, typed, or did something I probably shouldn't have and now I can't edit a box or page.

I am trying to put an embed link into my libguide, and when I went to put it into the HTML code and saved it, it would be blank. 

Why don't I see my peer's name when I try to add them as a guide editor?

If you do not see someone's name this means that their account was not set up properly. Try having them check their account information by clicking their email address in the top right hand corner. Here they can change their settings. On this page their first and last name MUST be filled in in order to be visible in the guide editors screen.

 

 

I clicked, typed, or did something I probably shouldn't have and now I can't edit a box or page.

If you can no longer edit the page (can't even delete the page) this answer may be for you. Unfortunately, what I would do is create a new guide from scratch. For the pages select reuse existing page and reuse these pages you’ve already created. Click “copy” when you create the pages so you can edit them fro the new guide. If you can't copy the page, unfortunately, you will have to redo that page by copying text, images, etc. This seems like the best alternative to this issue. This has happened to me before when some code was put into one of my boxes that set the whole page astray.

 

 

I am trying to put an embed link (something like this, https://archive.org/details/lowellcourierjanjun_1850_01_roll14) into my libguide, and when I went to put it into the HTML code and saved it, it would be blank. 

 

The first option:

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://archive.org/details/lowellcourierjanjun_1850_01_roll14" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This one actually shows the webpage with a scroll bar and is just a variance of the incorrect code given.

The second option:

<iframe src='https://archive.org/stream/lowellcourierjanjun_1850_01_roll14?ui=embed#page/n0/mode/2up' width='480px' height='430px' frameborder='0' ></iframe>

This one just shows the journal; it’s a bit more aesthetically pleasing.

You can also change the width and height in pixels on both of these by just changing the number in the embed code. Or even, just by changing the “2up” in the second link to “1up” you will see some difference.
Getting the Most from Groups

Groups allow you to add custom headers, footers, color schemes and layouts to your LibGuides. The library uses Resource Blueprint Template as a Group. This gives the group it's header, blue box header scheme, and side navigation color scheme.
Color code checker

box.name: How do I create a Group?

asset.description:
1. Go to Admin > Groups.

2. Click + Add Group > Complete the form.
There are 3 types of groups:

  • Public: Indexed; Available to all.
  • Restricted: Indexed; Available to all in the designated IP range and/or with the password.
  • Internal: Not indexed; Available only to those with accounts in the system.

3. Click Save.

box.name: How do I edit my Group?

asset.description:
Once you have created your Group, click on the pencil/paper icon to edit the Group.

You can customize each of these pages with: 

  • Banner - use a different image to highlight what these guides represent.
  • Custom JS/CSS Code - if you're code savvy, you can change things like colors, fonts, and more! 
  • Color Picker - don't know CSS? No problem! You can change the background & box colors using our built-in color picker.
  • Templates - just like at the system-level, you can create custom templates for the group's homepage and guides.
  • Language Options - want to change the wording of a few labels or create a group of guides in a different language? Go for it!

To top it off, each group has its own User Access settings. You choose who can access the group - is it for the general public? Staff members? Student staff? You choose! You can also control which account holders have access to the group settings - you don't have to manage them alone!
Under the general tab you can change your Group Name, description, URL and Group Type at any time.

When you add a new account on LibGuides you grant access to edit and work with certain groups. At any time as an admin you can change which groups a user can use by going directly to their account information. You can also grant access to users from the Group page by going to the User Access tab. Here you can add users to the group and change their privileges (regular, admin or no access).

Under Header / Footer / Tabs / Boxes you can:

  • Upload a custom Header
  • Set a Group Footer
  • Customize the color scheme and box shape for Tabs and Boxes

Under the header/footer/tabs/boxes tab your first option is to add a custom header. You are going to want to exclude the system level header by checking that first box. You can then upload an image from your computer. The width of the screen is 1170 px. You want to make sure your image is long and thin enough for use as a header.

You can also add HTML text under this header. This has not been implemented in the Resource Blueprint Template. This same process repeats itself for the footer. There is currently no footer for the Resource Blueprint Group.

Your next option is to change the style of the boxes and tabs. This screen is similar to the one inside your LibGuide edit page, where you can change the box and tab options there as well on an individual guide basis. The Resource Blueprint Template does not customize these options here. You can also check at the bottom if you want to lock all of the guides in this group. This would restrict these guides so that the editor would not be able to change the tab and box settings from within the guide.

The Custom Code tab allows you to insert your own JS/CSS code to change the settings for your group. These changes can include header font options, header display options, guide title font, etc. The Resource Blueprint code is explained below so that when you want to add a new group you can change this code and tailor it to your own group:

The code is split up into sections, where parts are highlighted and explained (color coded)

<style>
/* Header */
#s-lib-banner.container { width:100%; background: url('https://s3.amazonaws.com/libapps/customers/10/images/UML-libguide-header-bkgd-1px168px.png') repeat-x; } 
#s-lib-banner-img { width:1170px; display:block; margin-left:auto; margin-right:auto; }
#s-lg-public-skiplink { top: -45px; }

This changes the percentage of the top of the screen the banner takes up. Leave this at 100%

This changes the width of the image that is used as the banner. If you make this smaller the banner will shrink to that width and colors will emerge on either side to fill the rest of the screen. Leave this at the full width.

/* Font colors */
body, .s-lib-box { color: #333; font-size:14px; }
a { color: #02589f; }
a:hover, a:active { color: #5c6e7c; }

This section changes the font colors. 

This changes the color of your font that you have not already edited. For example, if you add rich text and change the font style, color, size, etc within your guide this code does not effect it. This code effects unedited code, tab names, footer text, etc. 

/* Formatting the guide title font */
h1#s-lg-guide-name { text-transform: uppercase; font-size:24px; font-family: Tahoma, Geneva, sans-serif; }

Here you can change the Guide title font options. Changing the text-transform to lowercase makes the title lowercase. If you delete this, the title will look exactly how you entered it when you named the guide. You can also change the font size of the title, the font family and type. There are only a couple of font family's that the site owns (Verdana, Georgia, Tahoma, Arial, Comic Sans, Courier New, Lucida Sans Unicode, Times New Roman). This is the first word of the font-family. The second after the comma (noted here as Geneva) is the type face within the first font listed. 

/* Spacing for elements on the page */
h3 { font-size: 18px; margin-top:15px; margin-bottom:0; }
div#s-lg-guide-header-info { margin-top: 30px; margin-bottom:10px; }

This changes the spacing between the header and the guide title. 

This changes the spacing between the guide title and the boxes and side navigation panel.

/* Side-Nav Button Formatting */
#s-lg-tabs-container .nav-pills > li > a {     font-family: Tahoma, Arial, sans-serif;     font-size: 17px;     font-weight:normal;     color: #6f8597;     line-height:34px;     padding: 4px 15px;     border:0; }
#s-lg-tabs-container .nav-pills > li { margin-top:1px; }
#s-lg-tabs-container .nav-pills > .active > a, #s-lg-tabs-container .nav-pills > .active > a:hover, #s-lg-tabs-container .nav-pills > li > a:hover {     background-color:#deecf6;      border-left:12px solid #02589f;     border-top:0;     border-bottom:0;     font-weight:normal;     color: #02589f;     padding: 4px 15px; }

Above this changes the side-navigation format similar to that discussed above. You can change the font, size, weight (bold, etc), color, padding, border of both the page names and the page names as you hover over the name. 

/* Forcing box titles to display - the system isn't allowing it. */
.s-lib-box h2.s-lib-box-title { display: block!important; }

/* Forcing box titles in row 2 to not display, as the title in row 1 takes care of that, so it can span the screen.Also changing the spacing so the box content displays closer to the row 1 box title, so they look connected. */
#welcome-row-header #s-lg-col-1 .s-lib-box { margin:0; }
#welcome-row-content .s-lib-box h2.s-lib-box-title { display:none!important; }
#welcome-row-content .s-lib-box-content { padding-top:0; }

If you want columns 2 and 3 to display headers you can delete this section of the code

/* Box look & feel changes to get the dark blue / gray effect in the header */
.s-lib-box { border-width:1px; border-color:#fff; box-shadow:none; }
.s-lib-box h2.s-lib-box-title { border-left:12px solid #02589f; color:#333; border-bottom:0; background-color:#deecf6; text-transform:uppercase; font-size:17px; font-weight:normal; line-height:30px; }
.s-lib-box-content { padding: 10px 0; }

/* Box content look & feel changes*/
  /* Making the first h3 in a box have no top margin, so it aligns to the top of the box / the boxes next to it. */
  div.s-lib-box-content h3:first-child { margin-top:0; }

</style>

Page Layout is where you change the general look of the page organization scheme. For example, do you want to have 6 different box sizes, different box ratios, etc? This is where templates come into play. See here for more information.

Here you do not need to change anything (most likely). You are going to want to leave the language as english (default).

If you want to change some of the wording even if the language base is english you can customize. For more information see here.
A template is where you change the layout of your guide. You can change the arrangement of boxes, sizes of boxes, etc. This is found under Groups.
For more help see this Springshare Page on Templates.

box.name: How to change Your Guide Template

asset.description:
Templates can be found under Page Layout in your Group edit page. 

There are two main types of layouts: side nav and top nav. The system comes with a default for each of these: System Default - Tab Layout, System Default - Side-Nav Layout. At UML Library a template has been created that uses the side-nav layout, this is the Resource Blueprint Template (note, you do not need to be in the Resource Blueprint group to use the Resource Blueprint Template).

If you want to make your own template you can do this by selecting "Customize Guide Template"

WARNING: DO NOT CHANGE TEMPLATE SETTINGS IF YOU DO NOT KNOW HTML CODING. THIS IS BEST LEFT TO SOMEONE WHO CAN CODE SO THAT UNWANTED CHANGES DO NOT OCCUR WITHIN THE SYSTEM.

In the Customize Guide Template tab you can select the template you want to 1) edit and save or 2) make a copy of and save as a new template. 

 

 

 

Once you select which template you would like to use you will see the code for that template. Here you can change the code.

 

IMPORTANT: IF YOU DID NOT CREATE THIS TEMPLATE DO NOT EDIT IT AND SAVE CHANGES TO THE TEMPLATE, INSTEAD, SAVE AS A NEW TEMPLATE.

box.name: Top Social Work Journals - Browse Online!

asset.description:
Top journals about social work - available online!

If the journal you want to access is not listed here, go back to the Library home page and look for the link to Journals search on the far right below the Quick Search Box. Type in the exact title including of, the, etc (i.e. Journal of the American Academy of Child Psychiatry) and see if we have access. If you do not find the journal you need, Ask a Librarian.

asset.name: Journal of Global Social Work Practice
asset.description: JSWGC is a peer reviewed journal and recognizes that social work is a global phenomenon with a myriad of contributors and perspectives. The journal is open to social work practice and research both domestically and abroad.

asset.name: Journal of Social Service Research
asset.description: The Journal of Social Service Research is exclusively devoted to empirical research and its application to the design, delivery, and management of the new social services. The Journal focuses on outcomes-based research and practice, and clearly presents the different types of funded and non-funded state-of-the-art research being carried out in the field. Each issue effectively highlights both the quantitative and qualitative methodologies. Contributors from the national and international social service arenas provide an important and critical basis for management and policy decisions in a wide variety of social service settings.

asset.name: Journal of Social Work Education
asset.description: A quarterly journal that provides a forum for the exchange of social work information among professionals and academics.

asset.name: Journal of Social Work Values & Ethics
asset.description: The JSWVE examines the ethical and values issues that impact and are interwoven with social work practice, research, and theory development. JSWVE addresses ethical and value issues that encompass the full range of social problems and issues that social workers encounter. The journal provides the necessary historical perspectives on the development of social work values and ethics, as well as present articles providing value and ethical dilemmas stemming from state-of-the-art developments.

asset.name: Smith College Studies in Social Work
Social Work in Health Care
asset.description: Devoted to social work theory, practice, and administration in a wide variety of health care settings, this journal gives you the tools to improve your practice while keeping you up-to-date with the latest crucial information. Social Work in Health Care is edited by Gary Rosenberg, PhD, one of the most respected leaders in health social work. This creative, lively journal brings you the most important articles on research, leadership, clinical practice, management, education, collaborative relationships, social health policy, and ethical issues from the most respected experts in the field. The journal's special issues comprehensively discuss a single pertinent health care theme.

Professional organizations can be a great source of information about careers.  Many organizations have job postings, links to scholarship applications, and information about certification requirements, graduate schools, and more.  They may also provide access to reports and research in the field.  If the report you find is not fully available on the organization's webiste, ask at the library!

asset.name: Association of Social Work Boards
asset.description: The Association of Social Work Boards (ASWB) is the association of boards that regulate social work. ASWB develops and maintains the social work licensing examinations and is a central resource for information on the legal regulation of social work. ASWB is also available to help individual social workers and social work students with questions they may have.

asset.name: National Association of Social Workers
asset.description: The National Association of Social Workers provides news items of interest to social workers, links to career information and job postings, services for finding social workers, and more.

asset.name: Social Work Policy Institute
asset.description: The Social Work Policy Institute examines and reports upon issues that relate to the work of social workers, including how to serve people who have multiple or complex needs and how public agencies and other structures deliver health and human services.

box.name: Find on the Shelf: New Arrivals

asset.name: We Were Feminists Once
asset.description: Feminism has hit the big time. Once a dirty word brushed away with a grimace, "feminist" has been rebranded as a shiny label sported by movie and pop stars, fashion designers, and multi-hyphenate powerhouses like Beyonc#65533;. It drives advertising and marketing campaigns for everything from wireless plans to underwear to perfume, presenting what's long been a movement for social justice as just another consumer choice in a vast market. Individual self-actualization is the goal, shopping more often than not the means, and celebrities the mouthpieces. But what does it mean when social change becomes a brand identity? Feminism's splashy arrival at the center of today's media and pop-culture marketplace, after all, hasn't offered solutions to the movement's unfinished business. Planned Parenthood is under sustained attack, women are still paid 77 percent-or less-of the man's dollar, and vicious attacks on women, both on- and offline, are utterly routine. Andi Zeisler, a founding editor of Bitch Media, draws on more than twenty years' experience interpreting popular culture in this biting history of how feminism has been co-opted, watered down, and turned into a gyratory media trend. Surveying movies, television, advertising, fashion, and more, Zeisler reveals a media landscape brimming with the language of empowerment, but offering little in the way of transformational change. Witty, fearless, and unflinching, We Were Feminists Once is the story of how we let this happen, and how we can amplify feminism's real purpose and power.
asset.author: Andi Zeisler

asset.name: Bad Girls of the Arab World
asset.description: Women's transgressive behaviors and perspectives are challenging societal norms in the Arab world, giving rise to anxiety and public debate. Simultaneously, however, other Arab women are unwillingly finding themselves labeled "bad" as authority figures attempt to redirect scrutiny from serious social ills such as patriarchy and economic exploitation, or as they impose new restrictions on women's behavior in response to uncertainty and change in society. Bad Girls of the Arab World elucidates how both intentional and unintentional transgressions make manifest the social and cultural constructs that define proper and improper behavior, as well as the social and political policing of gender, racial, and class divisions. The works collected here address the experiences of women from a range of ages, classes, and educational backgrounds who live in the Arab world and beyond. They include short pieces in which the women themselves reflect on their experiences with transgression; academic articles about performance, representation, activism, history, and social conditions; an artistic intervention; and afterwords by the acclaimed novelists Laila al-Atrash and Miral al-Tahawy. The book demonstrates that women's transgression is both an agent and a symptom of change, a site of both resistance and repression. Showing how transnational forces such as media discourses, mobility and confinement, globalization, and neoliberalism, as well as the legacy of colonialism, shape women's badness, Bad Girls of the Arab World offers a rich portrait of women's varied experiences at the boundaries of propriety in the twenty-first century.
asset.author: Nadia Yaqub (Editor); Rula Quawas (Editor)

asset.name: I Am Not a Slut
asset.description: The author of the groundbreaking work Slut! explores the phenomenon of slut-shaming in the age of sexting, tweeting, and "liking." She shows that the sexual double standard is more dangerous than ever before and offers wisdom and strategies for alleviating its destructive effects on young women's lives. Young women are encouraged to express themselves sexually. Yet when they do, they are derided as "sluts." Caught in a double bind of mixed sexual messages, young women are confused. To fulfill the contradictory roles of being sexy but not slutty, they create an "experienced" identity on social media-even if they are not sexually active--while ironically referring to themselves and their friends as "sluts." But this strategy can become a weapon used against young women in the hands of peers who circulate rumors and innuendo--elevating age-old slut-shaming to deadly levels, with suicide among bullied teenage girls becoming increasingly common. Now, Leora Tanenbaum revisits her influential work on sexual stereotyping to offer fresh insight into the digital and face-to-face worlds contemporary young women inhabit. She shares her new research, involving interviews with a wide range of teenage girls and young women from a variety of backgrounds as well as parents, educators, and academics. Tanenbaum analyzes the coping mechanisms young women currently use and points them in a new direction to eradicate slut-shaming for good.
asset.author: Leora Tanenbaum

asset.name: Funding Feminism
asset.description: Joan Marie Johnson examines an understudied dimension of women's history in the United States: how a group of affluent white women from the late nineteenth through the mid-twentieth centuries advanced the status of all women through acts of philanthropy. This cadre of activists included Phoebe Hearst, the mother of William Randolph Hearst; Grace Dodge, granddaughter of Wall Street "Merchant Prince" William Earle Dodge; and Ava Belmont, who married into the Vanderbilt family fortune. Motivated by their own experiences with sexism, and focusing on women's need for economic independence, these benefactors sought to expand women's access to higher education, promote suffrage, and champion reproductive rights, as well as to provide assistance to working-class women. In a time when women still wielded limited political power, philanthropy was perhaps the most potent tool they had. But even as these wealthy women exercised considerable influence, their activism had significant limits. As Johnson argues, restrictions tied to their giving engendered resentment and jeopardized efforts to establish coalitions across racial and class lines. As the struggle for full economic and political power and self-determination for women continues today, this history reveals how generous women helped shape the movement. And Johnson shows us that tensions over wealth and power that persist in the modern movement have deep historical roots.
asset.author: Joan Marie Johnson

asset.name: Why Congress Needs Women
asset.description: This book addresses women's civil strategies for negotiation and leadership through careful analysis of social science research and management theory as well as interviews with women legislators, documenting how women in Washington are affecting the development of the world at all levels. * Addresses how women in Washington have redefined leadership and power in terms of how they listen, work collaboratively, negotiate, facilitate change, communicate effectively, and empower and mentor others * Identifies differences in the evidenced personal ethics between the genders in Congress that are reflective of their characters and professionalism--or lack thereof * Provides examples of the unusual bipartisanship and civility can be seen in the informal "sisterhood" that women senators and representatives have established that allows for more mature and cooperative relationships
asset.author: Michele A. Paludi (Editor)

asset.name: Feminism: a very short introduction
asset.description: This book provides an historical account of feminism, exploring its earliest roots as well as key issues including voting rights, the liberation of the sixties, and its relevance today. Margaret Walters touches on the difficulties and inequities that women still face more than forty years after the 'new wave' of 1960s feminism, such as how successful women are at combining domesticity, motherhood, and work outside the house. She brings the subject completely up to date by providing an analysis of the current situation of women across the globe, from Europe and the United States to Third World countries.
asset.author: Margaret Walters

asset.name: Routledge Critical Dictionary of Feminism and Postfeminism
asset.description: This authoritative new work is probably the widest-ranging reference on feminism ever to be published in paperback. Approachable for general readers as well as for students in women's studies-related courses at all levels, this invaluable guide follows the unique Critical Dictionary format in combining over a dozen in-depth background chapters with more than 400 A-Z dictionary entries. The background chapters are written by major voices in the field of feminist studies, and include thorough coverage of the history of feminism, as well as extensive discussions of topics such as Post-Feminism, Men in Feminism, Feminism and New Technologies, Feminism and Philosophy, and much more. The dictionary entries cover the major individuals and issues essential to an understanding both of feminism's roots and of the trends that are shaping its future. Readers will find entries on people like Aphra Behn, Simone de Beauvoir, Princess Diana, Courtney Love and Robert Bly, and on subjects such as Afro-American feminism, cosmetic surgery, the "new man", prostitution, reproductive technologies, "slasher" films, and much more.
asset.author: Sarah Gamble

asset.name: The Reader's Companion to U. S. Women's History
asset.description: The most inclusive book to date on U.S. women's collective history! A landmark work, The Reader's Companion to U.S. Women's History, gathers together more than 400 articles to offer a diverse, rich, and often neglected panorama of the nation's past. Written by more than 300 contributors, drawn from various areas of expertise, these narrative and interpretive entries "effectively cover five centuries of women's experiences" (Bloomsbury Review). Here are articles on cowgirls and child care, on the daily lives of single women and the changing notions of motherhood, on the artistic contributions of women of color and the history of Jewish feminism. Wide-ranging in scope and wonderfully accessible, this unique resource reexamines with fresh clarity and brio the issues and concerns that color the lives of all women. Articles and their contributors include: African American Women, Darlene Clark Hine; Cult of Domesticity, Carroll Smith-Rosenberg; Fashion and Style, Lynn Yaeger; Jazz and Blues, Daphne Duval Harrison; Lesbians, Elizabeth Lapovsky Kennedy; Native American Cultures, Clara Sue Kidwell; Picture Brides, Judy Yung; Salem Witchcraft Trials, Mary Beth Norton; Vietnam Era, Sara M. Evans.
asset.author: Wilma P. Mankiller (Editor); Gwendolyn Mink (Editor); Marysa Navarro (Editor); Barbara Smith (Editor); Gloria Steinem (Editor)

asset.name: Political and Historical Encyclopedia of Women
asset.description: First Published in 2003. Routledge is an imprint of Taylor & Francis, an informa company.
asset.author: Christine Fauré (Editor)

asset.name: Encyclopedia of Feminist Theories
asset.description: This volume offers a multidisciplinary insight into the complex field of feminist thought. It contains over 500 commissioned from an international team of contributors and includes explanations of key themes and ideas. Each entry contains cross references and a bibliographic guide to further reading. Over 50 biographical entries provide readers with a sense of how the theories they encounter have developed out of the lives and situations of their authors. Areas covered include: traditional taxonomies of feminist theory (such as socialist thought); theoretical subdivisions (eg ecofeminism and feminist spirituality); and discipline-specific issues (such as philosophy and anthropology); the conceptual apparatus of gender theory (such as biologism); methodologies (such as deconstruction and narrative theory); intersections (with areas such asracial theory and queer theory); and political issues (such as citizenship and reproductive rights).
asset.author: Lorraine Code (Editor)

asset.name: The A-Z of Social Research
asset.description: `A detailed and valuable addition to the literature that will be a very useful resource for lecturers, as well as having a wide appeal among students' - Tim May, University of Salford Have you ever wondered what a concise, comprehensive book providing critical guidance to the whole expanse of social science research methods and issues might look like? The A-Z is a collection of 94 entries ranging from qualitative research techniques to statistical testing and the practicalities of using the Internet as a research tool. Alphabetically arranged in accessible, reader-friendly formats, the shortest entries are 800 words long and the longest are 3000. Most entries are approximately 1500 words in length and are supported by suggestions for further reading. The book: - Answers the demand for a practical, fast and concise introduction to the key concepts and methods in social research - Supplies students with impeccable information that can be used in essays, exams and research projects - Demystifies a field that students often find daunting This is a refreshing book on social research methods, which understands the pressures that modern students face in their work-load and seeks to supply an authoritative study guide to the field. It should fulfil a long-standing need in undergraduate research methods courses for an unpatronising, utterly reliable aid to making sense of research methods.
asset.author: John D. Brewer (Editor); Robert L. Miller (Editor)

asset.name: National Women's Studies Organization (NWSA)
asset.description: Established in 1977, NWSA is a professional organization dedicated to leading the field of women's studies and gender studies, as well as its teaching, learning, research, and service wherever they be found.

asset.name: National Women's Organization (NOW)
asset.description: The National Organization for Women (NOW) is the largest organization of feminist activists in the United States. NOW has 500,000 contributing members and 550 chapters in all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Since its founding in 1966, NOW's goal has been to take action to bring about equality for all women.

asset.name: Feminist Majority Foundation (FMF)
asset.description: The Feminist Majority Foundation (FMF), which was founded in 1987, is a cutting edge organization dedicated to women's equality, reproductive health, and non-violence. In all spheres, FMF utilizes research and action to empower women economically, socially, and politically.

asset.name: AAUW
asset.description: AAUW (formerly known as the American Association of University Women) is nationwide network of more than 100,000 members and donors, 1,000 branches, and 500 college/university institution partners. For more than 128 years, AAUW members have examined and taken positions on the fundamental issues of the day — educational, social, economic, and political.
View a selection of our Manuscripts and University Archives online in our Digital Collections.

asset.name: Emma Bell Miles Southern Appalachia art and correspondence
asset.description: The Emma Bell Miles Southern Appalachia art and correspondence digital collection contains correspondence among members and friends of writer and artist Emma Bell Miles’ family of origin illustrating the personal roots of themes Emma lived out and developed in her work. The heart of the collection is a series of letters written during 1901-1903 concerning Emma’s troubled relationship with her parents, her life as a young woman, and her life as an emerging artist and naturalist; as well as the death of her mother, Emma’s marriage to Frank Miles soon thereafter, and disposition of Bell family property in Walden Ridge, Tennessee. The collection also features numerous examples of Emma's art, including watercolors, oil paintings, and sketches.
asset.author: Miles, Emma Bell, 1879-1919

asset.name: Penelope Johnson Allen Brainerd Mission correspondence and photographs
asset.description: The Penelope Johnson Allen Brainerd Mission correspondence and photographs digital collection features orignal correspondence and receipts created by the United States Department of War, Indian Agent Return J. Meigs, and Brainerd Mission superintendents and founders Gideon Blackburn, Cyrus Kingsbury, and Ard Hoyt. The collection also includes photographs of portraits of the Brainerd missionaries, Daughters of the American Revolution dedication events at Brainerd Mission Cemetery, and copies of etchings of Brainerd Mission.
asset.author: Allen, Penelope Johnson (1886-1985)

asset.name: Chattanooga Women's Oral Histories
asset.description: The Chattanooga Women's Oral Histories digital collection features interviews with women in and around Chattanooga, Tennessee. Interviewees were asked questions such as "What are some of your early memories of Chattanooga?" and "What do you perceive to be the core elements of a successful city?" The interviews celebrate the accomplishments and experiences of women business leaders, advocates, educators, social activists, and community builders across generation, socioeconomic, and cultural backgrounds.
Conduct primary source research with our manuscripts, which include collections of personal papers, diaries, photographs, ephemera, and business records.

asset.name: Andrews Family correspondence, photographs, and papers
asset.description: The Andrews Family correspondence, photographs, and papers collection includes correspondence, manuscripts, personal papers, geneologies, and photographs created by several generations of this family, who lived in Georgia and Chattanooga, Tennessee in the 18th and 19th centuries. Of particular interest is the journal of Eliza Frances Andrews (1840-1939), daughter of Judge Andrews. Eliza Andrews wrote several books, articles and essays (under her own name and using pseudonyms Fanny Andrews and Elzey Hay), including the popular War Time Journal of a Georgia Girl, 1864-1865 (D. Appleton and Co., 1908), A Family Secret (as Elzy Hay) (Lippincott, 1876) and several botany text books. Her journal documents the South during Reconstruction from 1870 to 1872.
asset.author: Andrews, Eliza Frances, 1840- ; Hay, Elzey, 1840-1939

asset.name: Anne Bachman Hyde correspondence and research notes
asset.description: The Anne Bachman Hyde correspondence and research notes s collection contains research notes, photographs, original documents, local histories, books, journals, newspaper clippings, and other materials relating to the Cherokee Indians and Brainerd Mission, Civil War, and United Daughters of the Confederacy, ranging from 1868 to 1959. The collection also features papers relating to Charles McGuffey, a Chattanooga, Tennessee lawyer and local historian and McGuffey's grandfather, Daniel Drake, a noted physician.
asset.author: Hyde, Anne Bachman, 1868-1959

asset.name: Caroline Gordon clippings, articles, and short stories
asset.description: The Caroline Gordon clippings, articles, and short stories collection contains newspaper clippings, journal articles, and short stories authored by and about the novelist and literary critic dating from 1933 to 1956.
asset.author: Gordon, Caroline, 1895-1981

asset.name: Jean Miles Catino and Emma Bell Miles correspondence, journals, and papers
asset.description: The Jean Miles Catino and Emma Bell Miles correspondence, journals, and papers collection contains Catino's correspondence as well as journals, artwork, and photographs created by Emma Bell Miles, Catino's mother. The Emma Bell Miles content documents mountain life on Walden Ridge in the early 20th century.
asset.author: Catino, Jean Miles, 1903-2000; Miles, Emma Bell, 1879-1919

asset.name: Marilyn Lloyd papers and correspondence
asset.description: The Marilyn Lloyd papers and correspondence collection contains her congressional papers, letters from constituents, and committee records, that document her 20 year service as a member of the United States House of Representatives from Tennessee's third Congressional District from 1974 to 1994.
asset.author: Lloyd, Marilyn (1929-)

asset.name: Penelope Johnson Allen papers
asset.description: The Penelope Johnson Allen research notes, correspondence, and photographs collection contains research notes, histories, correspondence, documents, photographs regarding history of Brainerd Mission and the efforts of the Judge David Campbell Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution to preserve and memorialize the Brainerd Mission Cemetary dating from 1803 to 1990.
asset.author: Allen, Penelope Johnson (1886-1985)

asset.description: Use for full text options.

Naxos Music Library [NML] is the world´s largest online classical music library. Currently, it offers streaming access to more than 46,000 CDs with more than 653,000 tracks, standard and rare repertoire. Over 800 new CDs are added to the library every month.

The library offers the complete Naxos and Marco Polo catalogues plus the complete catalogues or selected titles from over 250 classical, jazz and world music labels with more labels joining every month. Classic pop and rock music as well as Chinese orchestral music are also represented.

NML can be accessed from any computer, anywhere, anytime. With the new iPhone / iPod Touch App subscribers can also access the service on the go.

The contents can be searched by composer, work, genre and label; by keyword search and by a sophisticated advanced search engine with up to 10 combined search criteria. In addition to allowing subscribers to listen to recordings, NML provides liner notes for most recordings. Listeners can create personalized playlists or use predefined Naxos Music Library playlists. For student around the world the library also offers playlists for graded music exams (ABRSM, Trinity/Guildhall) in various categories and grades.

Furthermore, a vast array of background information is available. Resources include:

  • Audio book transcriptions about the history of classical music and opera with listening examples.
  • Libretti and synopses of over 700 operas.
  • A pronunciation guide for composer and artist names.
  • A glossary.
  • An overview of important musical terms.
  • Work analyses and
  • Work details with instrumentation, publishers, duration, work information and available recordings.

Subscribers can also listen to classical music podcasts. A comprehensive online encyclopedia of classical music is in development.

box.name: Find on the Shelf: New Arrivals

asset.name: The Devil's Music: how Christians inspired, condemned, and embraced rock 'n'
asset.description: When rock 'n' roll emerged in the 1950s, ministers denounced it from their pulpits and Sunday school teachers warned of the music's demonic origins. The big beat, said Billy Graham, was "ever working in the world for evil." Yet by the early 2000s Christian rock had become a billion-dollar industry. The Devil's Music tells the story of this transformation. Rock's origins lie in part with the energetic Southern Pentecostal churches where Elvis, Little Richard, James Brown, and other pioneers of the genre worshipped as children. Randall J. Stephens shows that the music, styles, and ideas of tongue-speaking churches powerfully influenced these early performers. As rock 'n' roll's popularity grew, white preachers tried to distance their flock from this "blasphemous jungle music," with little success. By the 1960s, Christian leaders feared the Beatles really were more popular than Jesus, as John Lennon claimed. Stephens argues that in the early days of rock 'n' roll, faith served as a vehicle for whites' racial fears. A decade later, evangelical Christians were at odds with the counterculture and the antiwar movement. By associating the music of blacks and hippies with godlessness, believers used their faith to justify racism and conservative politics. But in a reversal of strategy in the early 1970s, the same evangelicals embraced Christian rock as a way to express Jesus's message within their own religious community and project it into a secular world. In Stephens's compelling narrative, the result was a powerful fusion of conservatism and popular culture whose effects are still felt today.
asset.author: Randall J. Stephens

asset.name: Music Assessment for Better Ensembles
asset.description: Assessment is central to ensemble music. Yet, teachers do not always have the expertise to harness its potential to improve rehearsals and performances, and promote and document student learning. Written specifically for band, choir, and orchestra teachers at all levels, this book contains allof the information necessary to design and use assessment in a thriving music classroom. The first section addresses foundations such as learning targets, metacognition, and growth mindset. Assessment jargon such as formative assessment, summative assessment, Assessment for Learning, self and peer assessment, and authentic assessment is clarified and illustrated with music examples.Readers will learn practical strategies for choosing which concepts to assess, which methods to use, and how to use results to provide accurate and effective feedback to students. The second section brings assessment fundamentals into the music room. Filled with practical advice, each chapter examines a different facet of musicianship. Sample assessments in all performance areas are provided, including music literacy, fundamentals and technique, terminology, interpretation,evaluation and critique, composition and improvisation, beliefs and attitudes, and more. There is an entire chapter devoted to tips for applying assessment and feedback strategies in rehearsals, which can result in a fresh and effective approach to performance preparation.The final section is an examination of grading practices in music classes. Readers will gain information about ensemble grades that communicate what students know and are able to do, rather than whether they remembered their black socks. A variety of approaches, including Standards-Based Grading,are evaluated in light of music teachers' unique situations. The book concludes with ways for music educators to take their first steps toward implementing these strategies in their own teaching, including the use of instructional technology. Assessing like an expert is possible, and this book is just what teachers need to get started.
asset.author: Brian P. Shaw

asset.name: Good Booty: love and sex, black & white, body and soul in American music‎
asset.description: NPR Best Books of 2017 In this sweeping history of popular music in the United States, NPR's acclaimed music critic examines how popular music shapes fundamental American ideas and beliefs, allowing us to communicate difficult emotions and truths about our most fraught social issues, most notably sex and race. In Good Booty, Ann Powers explores how popular music became America's primary erotic art form. Powers takes us from nineteenth-century New Orleans through dance-crazed Jazz Age New York to the teen scream years of mid-twentieth century rock-and-roll to the cutting-edge adventures of today's web-based pop stars. Drawing on her deep knowledge and insights on gender and sexuality, Powers recounts stories of forbidden lovers, wild shimmy-shakers, orgasmic gospel singers, countercultural perverts, soft-rock sensitivos, punk Puritans, and the cyborg known as Britney Spears to illuminate how eroticism--not merely sex, but love, bodily freedom, and liberating joy--became entwined within the rhythms and melodies of American song. This cohesion, she reveals, touches the heart of America's anxieties and hopes about race, feminism, marriage, youth, and freedom. In a survey that spans more than a century of music, Powers both heralds little known artists such as Florence Mills, a contemporary of Josephine Baker, and gospel queen Dorothy Love Coates, and sheds new light on artists we think we know well, from the Beatles and Jim Morrison to Madonna and Beyonc#65533;. In telling the history of how American popular music and sexuality intersect--a magnum opus over two decades in the making--Powers offers new insights into our nation psyche and our soul.
asset.author: Ann Powers

asset.name: Audio Production Tips: Getting the Sound Right at the Source
asset.description: Audio Production Tips: Getting the Sound Right at the Sourceprovides practical and accessible information detailing the production processes for recording today's bands. By demonstrating how to "get the sound right at the source," author Peter Dowsett lays the appropriate framework to discuss the technical requirements of optimizing the sound of a source. Through its coverage of critical listening, pre-production, arrangement, drum tuning, gain staging and many other areas of music production, Audio Production Tipsallows you to build the wide array of skills that apply to the creative process of music production. Broken into two parts, the book first presents foundational concepts followed by more specific production advice on a range of instruments. Key features: Important in-depth coverage of music theory, arrangement and its applications. Real life examples with key references to the author's music production background. Presents concepts alongside the production of a track captured specifically for the book. A detailed companion website, including audio, video, Pro Tools session files of the track recording process, and videos including accompanying audio that can be examined in the reader's DAW. Please visit the accompanying companion website, available at www.audioproductiontips.com, for resources that further support the book's practical approach.
asset.author: Peter Dowsett

asset.name: The Cambridge Companion to the Singer-Songwriter
asset.description: Most often associated with modern artists such as Bob Dylan, Elton John, Don McLean, Neil Diamond, and Carole King, the singer-songwriter tradition in fact has a long and complex history dating back to the medieval troubadour and earlier. This Companion explains the historical contexts, musical analyses, and theoretical frameworks of the singer-songwriter tradition. Divided into five parts, the book explores the tradition in the context of issues including authenticity, gender, queer studies, musical analysis, and performance. The contributors reveal how the tradition has been expressed around the world and throughout its history to the present day. Essential reading for enthusiasts, practitioners, students, and scholars, this book features case studies of a wide range of both well and lesser-known singer-songwriters, from Thomas d'Urfey through to Carole King and Kanye West.
asset.author: Katherine Williams (Editor); Justin A. Williams (Editor)

asset.name: Hip Hop Raised Me
asset.description: Hip Hop Raised Me is the definitive volume on the essence, experience, and energy that is hip hop, and its massive and enduring impact over the last forty years. It's packed with contact sheets, outtakes, and glory shots of artists, collectives, and fans from iconic photographers including Martha Cooper, Henry Chalfant, Eddie Otchere, Normski, Janette Beckman, Chi Modu, Nabil Elderkin, and Mark Humphrey, as well as photographs of hip-hop ephemera and vinyl courtesy of specialist collectors. With the help of his definitive catalogue of interviews with hip-hop artists from the 1990s to today, conducted at key moments in their careers and including Jay-Z, Kanye West, Eminem, Macklemore & Ryan Lewis, Drake, Nicki Minaj, J Cole, Kendrick Lamar, Nas, and the Wu-Tang Clan, DJ Semtex examines the crucial role of hip hop in society. He reflects on the huge influence it has had on his own life and the lives of many others, providing inspiration to generation after generation of young people. Taking a thematic approach, Semtex traces the characteristics and influence of hip hop from its origins in the early 1970s with DJ Kool Herc's block parties in the South Bronx, through its breakthrough to the mainstream and advent of gangsta rap in the late 1980s, with artists such as Run DMC, Public Enemy, and Ice T, to the impact of contemporary artists and the global industry that is hip hop today.
asset.author: D. J. Semtex

asset.name: The Garland Encyclopedia of World Music
asset.description: The premiere volume of theGarland Encyclopedia of World Musicseries offers a comprehensive view of African music as a vital part of the social and cultural life of it peoples. The 34 expert contributors have all conducted fieldwork in Africa and their firsthand experience is reflected in the immediacy of their observations. In 39 articles, this encyclopedia explores key themes in African music that have emerged in recent years - a subject usually neglected in country-by-country coverage; emphasizes the contexts of musical performance-unlike studies that offer static interpretations isolated from other performing traditions; and presents the fresh insights and analyses of musicologists and anthropologists of diverse national origins-African, Asian, European and American. Also includes nine maps and 96 music examples.
asset.author: Ruth M. Stone (Editor)

asset.name: The New Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians
asset.description: Over 29,000 articles and more than 6,000 contributors from 98 countriesOver 20,000 biographies and more than 5,000 photographs, diagrams, drawings, and mapsCoverage of new schools of thought within musicology, such as feminism and gay and lesbian musicIncreased coverage of jazz and popular musicmeticulously cross-referencedThousands of musical examplesSpecially commissioned maps and line drawings Since its initial publication in 1980, the Dictionary has been widely acclaimed as an indispensable resource and a classic reference. The word 'updated' doesn't begin to describe the thousands of new articles, topics, cross-references, and areas of scholarship incorporated into The New Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians. Every one of the first edition's 22,500 articles has been reviewed and revised, with thousands of articles expanded. Previously neglected or under-represented areas have been examined, explored, and explained. Movements and topics once deemed too controversial or too far from the mainstream have been added. And throughout, 6,500 new articles cover more than 5,000 years of music history, instruments, composers, institutions, performers, genres, and more. The New Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians takes you beyond the customary and familiar into new worlds with extensive, authoritative contributions on non-Western music. From major influences, such as Latin American music, to less-examined contributions, such as Asian, sub-Saharan African, and Pacific Islander, The New Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians presents the music, theory, instruments, and musicians that have helped to define music around the world.
asset.author: Stanley Sadie (Editor); John Tyrrell (Editor)
